content_text: another good q that fits this framework "how do layoffs affect stock px" falls under arcana, reaction function, the tape shapes the news...no clear answer thats why it's a great question the best answer is in the form of, here's 6-7 variables where u can see that its all cross-currents and "it depends" -- 1. super high level 5% reduction in headcount --> opex goes down 5% --> earnings go up 5% --> stock goes up 5%. thats the monkey-math / "my model says so" answer 2. but usually, those humans had some future-revenue-generation component attached to them so future revenue has to come down by an offsetting % were they productive humans? unproductive humans? is AI replacing them? all of these are puts and takes in model forecast 3. then, you have to ask: "why do companies lay people off?" usually, it's because demand has declined, or they have some visibility into lower demand in the future this has to show up in your future revenue % somewhere. maybe it really is "100% AI redundancy" but u don't know 4. mgmt credibility this is a thing here too...a dogshit business that says "its AI redundancy," but where you know its a smokescreen and really a fxn of lower demand, that sways the calculus. 5. narrative narratives matter a company that has been growing like crazy, all systems go, adding headcount + opex etc, "get market share first and we'll be profitable later"...and then suddenly announces layoffs? there's informational content in there, and the mkt tends to interpret it correctly --> react extremely negatively...."stock is ex-growth" "best days are behind it" and so on 6. what are direct comps doing if all their peers are adding, and they're laying off, that should prob elicit a "wtf, something is wrong, sell" reaction 7. last, you also have broad macro are we in a boom or a bust? layoffs in oct 2008 are not the same as layoffs in a backdrop like today's (record high indices) -- summary: "clear as mud" you could prob keep hitting LLMs with this and get even more answers, but it falls under the same framework as all the "implied return on capex" questions that the market is grappling with sometimes px action holds the best answer...and even within that...sometimes "100 million frenchmen" get it wrong.
